case_notes:
# Case 1

68M, pancytopenic for three months, transfusion dependent. Marrow reported as MDS
with 12% blasts on the aspirate, dysplasia in two lineages. Normal karyotype on
20 metaphases.

NGS (myeloid panel, 54 genes):
- NPM1 c.863_864insTCTG p.(Trp288CysfsTer12), VAF 41%
- DNMT3A p.(Arg882His), VAF 46%
- FLT3-ITD, allelic ratio 0.38

structured_case.detected_variants_summary: NGS detected NPM1 c.863_864insTCTG p.(Trp288CysfsTer12) (VAF 41%), DNMT3A p.(Arg882His) (VAF 46%), and FLT3-ITD (allelic ratio 0.38).

case_facts.value: Pancytopenic for three months and transfusion dependent.
Marrow reported as MDS with 12% aspirate blasts and dysplasia in two lineages.

# NGS panel scope

This file defines the gene-level scope of the laboratory NGS panel used by this workflow.
It intentionally does not encode transcript, exon, or amplicon numbers.

## Negative-result semantics

When the patient NGS result is explicitly complete, a listed panel gene that is absent from the detected-variant list is interpreted as **no SNV, short insertion/deletion, or short-range complex variant detected in that gene within the validated assay scope**.

Use this negative result when applying diagnostic, prognostic, biomarker, treatment, germline, and other reporting rules. Do not treat the gene as unresolved merely because it is not individually listed in the patient result.

This inference is limited to the assay scope. It does not establish whole-gene biological wild type and does not exclude copy-number changes, rearrangements, structural variants, or other variant classes unless the patient result or another supplied test explicitly assesses them.

If the patient NGS result is described as partial, selected, limited, abbreviated, pending, or otherwise incomplete, do not infer a negative result for an unlisted panel gene.

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: CNL requires exclusion of BCR::ABL1-positive CML and myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine-kinase fusions.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: CEL, NOS requires absence of BCR::ABL1, other ABL1, PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, JAK2, or FLT3 tyrosine-kinase fusions.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diseases: myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and TK fusion
diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: FLT3 rearrangement defines an ICC genetic subtype of myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and a tyrosine-kinase fusion.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Identification of a tyrosine-kinase fusion associated with M/LN-eo excludes a diagnosis of systemic mastocytosis.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Development of an NPM1 mutation in established CMML should be noted but does not by itself define de novo AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: aCML requires absence of genetic abnormalities defining myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine-kinase fusions.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS-SF3B1 that later develops thrombocytosis is classified as thrombocytotic progression of MDS-SF3B1 rather than as MDS/MPN.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS/MPN with SF3B1 mutation and thrombocytosis requires absence of genetic abnormalities defining myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine-kinase fusions.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Neither dysplasia nor ring sideroblasts are required for the diagnosis of MDS-SF3B1 when the defining genetic criteria are met.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS-SF3B1 requires an SF3B1 mutation with VAF at least 10%.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS-SF3B1 requires absence of multi-hit TP53.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS-SF3B1 requires absence of a RUNX1 mutation.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS with del(5q) requires del(5q) to be isolated or accompanied by only one other cytogenetic abnormality, except -7/del(7q).
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS with del(5q) excludes multi-hit TP53.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS with mutated TP53 is defined in the 0%-9% blood or marrow blast range.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS with mutated TP53 requires multi-hit TP53.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: When TP53-locus LOH information is unavailable, a TP53 mutation with VAF above 10% plus complex karyotype is accepted for MDS with mutated TP53.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Two distinct TP53 mutations, each with VAF above 10%, establish multi-hit TP53.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: A TP53 mutation with a cytogenetic deletion involving the TP53 locus at 17p13.1 establishes multi-hit TP53.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: A single TP53 mutation with VAF above 50% establishes multi-hit TP53.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: A TP53 mutation with copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity at the 17p TP53 locus establishes multi-hit TP53.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Monoallelic TP53-mutated MDS is not included in the ICC MDS with mutated TP53 entity, which requires multi-hit TP53.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Acquisition of TP53 mutation during MDS progression can reclassify disease as MDS, MDS/AML, or AML with mutated TP53 according to blast count.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In germline RUNX1- or ETV6-associated platelet disorders, megakaryocytic dysplasia can occur without MDS and therefore should not by itself establish MDS.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In a germline-predisposition setting, emergence of multi-hit TP53 mutation with VAF above 10% is considered MDS-defining.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In a germline-predisposition setting, emergence of SF3B1 mutation with VAF above 10% is considered MDS-defining.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In Shwachman-Diamond syndrome, a small stable monoallelic TP53-mutant clone in isolation is not considered development of MDS.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: A RARA rearrangement involving NPM1 is included among APL with other RARA rearrangements, diagnosable with at least 10% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML with mutated NPM1 can be diagnosed with at least 10% blood or marrow blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: CDX2/UBTF B-ALL is defined by concomitant FLT3/PAN3-region enhancer retargeting with CDX2 deregulation and a UBTF-region lesion producing UBTF::ATXN7L3.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In MDS, TP53 multihit status is defined by multiple TP53 mutations or by a TP53 mutation with loss of heterozygosity, including chromosomal deletion or copy-neutral LOH.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: IPSS-M Prognostic score for MDS

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Mutated NPM1 is an AML-defining recurrent genetic abnormality when marrow or blood blasts are at least 10%.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), recurrent RARA rearrangements involving IRF2BP2, NPM1, ZBTB16, STAT5B, STAT3, TBL1XR1, FIP1L1, or BCOR should be reported as the specific RARA-rearranged entity; as AML-defining recurrent abnormalities, they apply at at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute myeloid leukemia (AML), the rare recurring rearrangements involving PRDM16::RPN1, RBM15::MRTFA, NPM1::MLF1, NUP98::NSD1, ETV6::MNX1, KAT6A::CREBBP, PICALM::MLLT10, NUP98::KMD5A or other NUP98 partners, FUS::ERG, RUNX1::CBFA2T3, and CBFA2T3::GLIS2 are AML-defining recurrent genetic abnormalities and apply at at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: ACD, CTC1, DKC1, MDM4, RTEL1, TERC, TERT, TINF2, NHP2, NOP10, NPM1, PARN, WRAP53, RPA1, and APOLLO are listed in Table 2 as genes associated with telomere biology disorders/short telomere syndromes and myeloid-neoplasm predisposition.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Table 2 identifies NPM1 as a gene associated with germline predisposition due to NPM1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants, associated with bone-marrow failure and B-cell deficiency; Table 2 lists this among emerging disorders based on limited published cases.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: When leukemia develops in germline RUNX1 predisposition, somatic mutation of the wild-type RUNX1 allele is common, together with acquired mutations in ASXL1, FLT3, GATA2, PHF6, SRSF2, and WT1.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For CCUS, MDS and MDS/MPN, cytopenia thresholds are haemoglobin <13 g/dL in males or <12 g/dL in females, ANC <1.8 ×10^9/L, and platelets <150 ×10^9/L.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS is defined by cytopenias and morphologic dysplasia, with a recommended dysplasia threshold of 10% for all lineages.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Within genetically defined MDS, MDS with biallelic TP53 inactivation supersedes MDS-5q and MDS-SF3B1 in the WHO5 hierarchy.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In MDS-5q, an SF3B1 mutation or a TP53 mutation that is not multi-hit does not by itself override the MDS-5q diagnosis.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For SF3B1-wild-type MDS with ≥15% ring sideroblasts, “MDS with low blasts and ring sideroblasts” remains an acceptable alternative designation.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: WHO5 retains a 20% blast cutoff to delineate MDS from AML while removing blast cutoffs for most AML types with defining genetic abnormalities.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In a suspected CMML case with eosinophilia, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with tyrosine-kinase gene fusions should be excluded by assessing for PDGFRA rearrangement (most commonly FIP1L1::PDGFRA), PDGFRB rearrangement (most commonly ETV6::PDGFRB), FGFR1 rearrangement, JAK2 rearrangement, FLT3 rearrangement, ETV6::ABL1, and other defined tyrosine-kinase fusions including ETV6::FGFR2, ETV6::LYN, ETV6::NTRK3, RANBP2::ALK, BCR::RET, and FGFR1OP::RET. WHO5 treats PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, JAK2 and FLT3 as rearrangement-defined categories rather than restricting them to a single fusion partner.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML with NPM1 mutation can be diagnosed irrespective of blast count, with clinicopathologic correlation.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For inherited bone-marrow-failure syndromes with germline predisposition to myeloid neoplasms, this review lists DKC1, DNAJC21, ELANE, EFL1, ERCC6L2, FANC genes, GFI1, HAX1, NAF1, NPM1, RAD51C, RECQL4, RTEL1, SBDS, SRP72, TERT, and TERC among genes recommended as yielding clinically actionable results.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Kraft & Godley 2020 Germline NGS Review

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In patients investigated for unexplained cytopenia, a negative result across the studied 40-gene panel did not exclude the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML): the negative predictive value was 0.76, increasing to 0.84 when mutation status was combined with standard karyotyping.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In patients investigated for unexplained cytopenia, finding two or more somatic mutations in the studied 40-gene panel was strongly predictive of the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML), with positive predictive value 0.88 (95% CI 0.84-0.92). These predictive findings were reported as fully confirmed in the independent 190-patient validation cohort.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For mutations measured in isolated peripheral-blood granulocytes, a VAF around 0.10 was associated with the best classification of the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML); the paper cautions that the applicable allele-burden threshold may vary when a different blood-cell source is used. These predictive findings were reported as fully confirmed in the independent 190-patient validation cohort.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In unexplained cytopenia, mutations in SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1, JAK2, or RUNX1 had the highest predictive values for the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML), with positive predictive values of 0.88-0.97 irrespective of co-occurring mutations. These predictive findings were reported as fully confirmed in the independent 190-patient validation cohort.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In unexplained cytopenia, isolated TET2, DNMT3A, or ASXL1 mutations were substantially less predictive of the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML) than the same mutations occurring with additional genetic lesions (positive predictive value 0.29-0.57 vs 0.81-0.89). These predictive findings were reported as fully confirmed in the independent 190-patient validation cohort.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For patients diagnosed with MDS on the basis of mild dysplasia (<25% dysplastic cells), absence of detectable clonality by standard cytogenetics and targeted sequencing, together with a stable course, raised concern that the MDS diagnosis might be inappropriate despite meeting then-current WHO criteria.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In cases with inconclusive dysplasia, highly specific mutation patterns may provide presumptive evidence of MDS even without definitive morphology. The reported patterns included splicing-factor mutations and co-mutation patterns involving TET2, ASXL1, or DNMT3A with RUNX1, EZH2, CBL, BCOR, CUX1, TP53, or IDH1/IDH2; SRSF2/U2AF1 with JAK2 in primary myelofibrosis was a stated specificity exception.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In MDS with del(5q), the chromosomal deletion itself can represent the founding and disease-defining genetic lesion.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: As restated from then-current WHO criteria, MDS diagnosis required unexplained cytopenia plus morphologic evidence of dysplasia and/or an MDS-specific cytogenetic abnormality.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation
